A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CLIPErase and are readable throughout, including equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The shared method and experiments can be matched reliably. v1 has a placeholder Appendix A; v2 contains substantive Appendices A–F.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-100 and Flickr30K experiments, module ablations, forget-class proportion tests, and embedding and attention visualizations.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on the retained benchmarks, Conceptual 12M, BLIP, and diffusion generation, plus additional analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same dot-product forgetting loss, contrastive retention loss, KL consistency loss, and weighted combination. The BLIP and diffusion applications reuse CLIPErase without documenting a changed unlearning algorithm. Revised loss weights are experimental settings.

E1.justification: Beyond v1's CIFAR-100 and Flickr30K prediction/retrieval coverage, v2 evaluates a 120,000-pair Conceptual 12M subset and adds text-to-image concept removal using Stable Diffusion. New generation scenarios include multiple coexisting concepts and selective removal of apple fruit while preserving Apple products.

E2.justification: The CIFAR-100 comparator set is retained. Flickr30K Table 3 adds EMMN, printed as CLIP+ENMN, which was absent from that comparison in v1. v2 Figure 1 also introduces a generation comparison against text-only gradient-ascent unlearning.

E3.justification: The main settings change from 50 epochs, batch size 32, and equal loss weights to 20 epochs, batch size 16, and weights (1,3,3). v2 adds BLIP and patch-14 configurations, a five-epoch Conceptual 12M protocol, and YOLOv5 detection evaluation with 50 captions per concept and 400 images per model. Main-text and appendix descriptions of training length and splits are partly inconsistent.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses across forget classes, patch sizes and model architectures, Conceptual 12M single- and multi-concept forgetting, and diffusion case studies of selective removal. The original module ablation and forget-proportion study remain. Appendix D Tables 9 and 11 report identical targets and scores, so they do not establish two distinct analyses.

E5.justification: v2 Table 7 newly reports means and variances across five forget-class choices, with further discussion in Appendix C. This measures variation across classes; it does not establish repeated-seed uncertainty. Neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Shared tables and robustness curves change substantially, alongside newly added results. For example, CLIPErase's CIFAR-100 retained prediction accuracy changes from 89.41% to 90.99%, while Flickr30K image-retrieval R@1 forget/retain scores change from 10.40/21.41 to 3.37/17.71. Baseline scores and rankings also change. The revised protocols prevent interpreting these as controlled same-setting gains or losses.

T1.justification: The problem definition and mathematical objectives remain equivalent; v2 expresses the contrastive loss using softmax notation. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs. The added detection-rate formula explains an evaluation metric rather than introducing new theory.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a three-module framework for selective association unlearning without retraining. v2 extends the main claims to demonstrated diffusion-generation applicability and sense-specific forgetting, particularly removing apple-fruit associations while preserving Apple-product associations.

C2.justification: v2 adds a rationale for contrastive retention over embedding MSE and interprets difficult classes such as Mountain through shared features and complex backgrounds. Its main limitations shift toward benchmark scarcity and embedding-model scope. The earlier feature-overlap concern remains partly represented in Appendix C, while the broader future-work discussion moves largely unchanged to Appendix F.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project/code access link, Conceptual 12M sampling and cleaning constraints, exact forget/retain sample counts, weight decay, and additional training details. Appendix A.6 supplies per-epoch runtimes, and Appendix D reports the larger forget-set runtime. These materially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's basic settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Conceptual 12M, BLIP/BLIP-2, latent diffusion, and YOLOv5, while removing several introductory citations. Related work more explicitly contrasts CLIPErase with MultiDelete and synthetic-sample CLIP unlearning as task-specific approaches. The overall machine-unlearning positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten around generation failures and ambiguous concepts, and the method explanations and conclusion are expanded or rewritten. Experiments are reorganized around tasks, baseline descriptions are consolidated, and the former main-text discussion moves to Appendix F within a newly structured supplement.

P2.justification: v2 adds diffusion image grids and several result tables, expands Table 2 by dataset, and restructures Table 3 from side-by-side tasks into stacked task blocks. The robustness chart is redrawn with its panels reversed. Attention examples are reduced, while the existing t-SNE visualization is resized and annotated rather than replaced by a new analysis.

improvement.justification: Broader evaluation, class-variability analysis, and added code/settings information strengthen v2. However, its Conceptual 12M prose disagrees with Table 2, and Section 5.3 claims retained-text R@10 exceeds KL despite Table 3 showing 46.52% versus 54.85%; v1's corresponding superiority claim had directional support. Conflicting protocol descriptions and duplicated Tables 9/11 further weaken the added evidence. These unresolved problems prevent a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
